summary: Corrupted base64 attachments and truncated buffers after SSE reconnect behind gzip proxy
description: Issue summary: Customer reports that large responses containing embedded base64 attachments (images and small binary blobs in JSON envelope) arrive corrupted or truncated after their web client performs an SSE reconnect while going through a corporate gzip-enabled reverse proxy. Impact: Multiple API responses from the customer's app are returning syntactically valid JSON but with base64 attachments that fail to decode (padding/length mismatch) and occasional truncated message tails. This breaks downstream processing for image attachments and causes user-visible errors in the customer's UI. Environment: Production, us-east, customer traffic flows through a managed reverse proxy that adds gzip compression and HTTP/2->1 conversion for some mobile clients. Observed at ~2–3% of streaming sessions for this customer and started after they upgraded proxy appliance software last week.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Create a long streaming SSE response containing a JSON envelope with a base64-encoded image as part of a 'attachments' array.
2) Put the client behind a gzip-enabled reverse proxy that performs HTTP/2 to HTTP/1 conversions and occasional connection coalescing.
3) Start the SSE stream, then force a short disconnect (simulate mobile network switch) and allow the client to resume/reconnect using session-resume semantics.

4) Observe that the resumed stream yields a JSON envelope where the base64 blob has incorrect length or truncated padding, and the final portion of the stream is sometimes missing or duplicated metadata entries.
observed_behavior: Attachments' base64 fields cannot be decoded with standard base64 libraries (invalid padding or unexpected end of input). Some resumed sessions show duplicated small metadata frames followed by a truncated binary blob. When client disables proxy (direct to Redwood), issue does not reproduce.
expected_behavior: SSE resume should stitch the byte stream such that JSON envelopes and embedded base64 attachments are intact and decode successfully. No corruption or truncation should occur across reconnect boundaries.
logs: serving-runtime: resume-envelope: session=abc123; last_sent_seq=482; resumed_at_seq=483; final_ack=ok
application: decode-error: base64.DecodeError: unexpected EOF at byte 4092
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 - Initial triage by CS (Aisha): confirmed reproducible for customer when proxy gzip enabled; flagged as P1 due to enterprise impact.
2026-03-10 - Eng (Lucas) replicated reduced test case in staging using managed proxy emulator that coalesces chunk boundaries; reproduced corrupted padding on resumed SSE stream.

2026-03-11 - Hypothesis: proxy gzip + chunk coalescing interacts with SSE resume offsets causing mismatch between logical resume offset and physical byte boundaries; base64 payloads crossing a coalesced boundary get re-chunked and on resume reconstruction the framing offsets used by our resume logic are no longer aligned with original JSON token boundaries.

2026-03-11 - Evidence: when disabling gzip on proxy the resume logic works; when introducing a small single-byte prefix to the base64 field the corruption shifts — consistent with offset misalignment rather than pure data loss.

2026-03-12 - Secondary hypothesis: HTTP/2 to HTTP/1 conversion in proxy rewrites chunk framing and may merge trailing keepalive heartbeats into previous chunk; our resume token uses byte offsets derived pre-compression which no longer map post-rewrite.
comments: Aisha Patel 2026-03-10: Customer reported failures starting after their proxy vendor pushed v3.1 firmware. They can reproduce reliably when that firmware is active. They've provided PCAP and edge logs (attached to ticket).

Lucas Nguyen 2026-03-11: I reproduced this in staging with a proxy emulator that performs gzip+frame-coalesce. It looks like resume offset is being interpreted against post-rewrite byte stream. Working on a minimal instrument to show byte mapping across proxy.
SRE On-Call (Marta Ruiz) 2026-03-12: Added temporary rate-limit bypass for the customer's dedicated pool to reduce retries while we debug; no service-wide impact.
Aisha Patel 2026-03-12: Customer accepted temporary mitigation (disable gzip on proxy) for testing but requests a permanent fix; they prefer a server-side hardening where possible.

Lucas Nguyen 2026-03-13: Draft PR created to add explicit resume framing metadata (per-message CRC and logical chunk boundary markers) to SSE envelopes to make resume tolerant to intermediate proxy rewriting. PR linked in related_github_prs.
root_cause: Interplay between reverse-proxy gzip compression + chunk coalescing and our SSE resume offset logic. Resume offsets were treated as byte positions in the post-compression stream, but proxies that rewrite framing (gzip or HTTP/2 conversion) change how bytes are presented on reconnect, causing misalignment that corrupts embedded base64 boundaries.
resolution: Partial workaround provided to customer: disable gzip rewriting on their reverse proxy, or configure proxy to preserve chunk boundaries (recommendation provided). Engineering has implemented a defensive change (instrumented in PR) to include per-envelope 16-bit CRC and explicit logical chunk markers so resume can verify/realign after reconnect. Full rollout planned after QA; ETA for canary: 2026-03-20.
follow_up_actions: 1) Engineering to land PR adding per-envelope CRC and logical chunk markers (PR #2784) and run end-to-end tests with multiple proxy appliances.
2) Product/Docs: update streaming resume runbook and include guidance for proxies (gzip, h2->h1 conversion) that can break resume semantics.
3) SRE: Add monitoring alert for increased base64 decode errors per-customer to detect regressions.
4) CS: Confirm with customer after canary rollout and coordinate rollback plan if issues persist.
